Our Mission

Knowledge that leads to healthier choices.

Empowering students to build healthier, drug-free communities through leadership, education, and prevention.

Why Our Organization Serves

What miseducation costs us, and what public health can do about it

Case Study

The Gaps We Address

📉
The Gap

A Crisis Fed by Miseducation

Fentanyl is a synthetic opioid up to 50 times stronger than heroin, and it now appears in counterfeit pills made to look like Xanax, Percocet, or Adderall. Many people who die from fentanyl never intended to take it at all — they believed they were taking something else entirely, often because prevention education never reached them in time.

🫁
The Medicine

Why It's So Dangerous

Fentanyl binds rapidly to opioid receptors in the brainstem that control breathing, which can cause respiratory depression within minutes. Because it's so potent, the margin between an active dose and a fatal one is extremely small — and counterfeit pills are rarely mixed evenly, so one pill from a batch can be far stronger than the next.

🏫
The Human Cost

Who's Actually Affected

Overdose deaths involving fentanyl have risen sharply among teenagers and young adults over the past several years — a population that, in many school systems, receives little or no updated education on counterfeit pills and synthetic opioids. Families are often left blindsided, unaware their child ever encountered the drug at all.

💊
The Response

What Public Health Can Do

Evidence-based approaches include widespread naloxone access and training, fentanyl test strip distribution, Good Samaritan laws that encourage bystanders to call for help, and honest, non-stigmatizing education about counterfeit pills — delivered before a first exposure, not after.

🤝
Takeaway

Why NSPN Exists

This is the gap NSPN chapters are built to close — translating current research on crises like this into honest, peer-led conversations that reach students before misinformation, or silence, does it for us.

This is an illustrative example for educational purposes, based on general public health research.

NSPN develops highly informative case studies on substance use and delivers them to high schools nationwide, equipping students with accurate, evidence-based information and opening honest conversations about substance abuse.

Our approach

Prevention works better when it comes from someone you trust.

Prevention First

We build every workshop and campaign from current research — not scare tactics or outdated slogans.

Peer-to-Peer Trust

College mentors train high school leaders. High school leaders run the room — student to student, not adult to teenager.

Nationally Connected

What works in one chapter gets documented and shared with every other chapter, coast to coast.

Where NSPN Started

NSPN started with a simple observation: most substance-prevention programs are designed by adults, for teenagers, and rarely land the way they’re supposed to. We flip that model. College chapters research the science, then work directly with high school chapter leaders to turn it into case studies and conversations that actually resonate with their peers. What began as a handful of campus chapters sharing curriculum with nearby high schools has grown into a nationwide network built on one idea: prevention works better when it comes from someone you trust.

SAMHSA Strategic Prevention Framework Trained

Every NSPN board member completes training in SAMHSA’s Strategic Prevention Framework (SPF) — the five-step, evidence-based planning process (assessment, capacity, planning, implementation, and evaluation) that the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration developed to guide prevention work nationwide. Completing SPF training is a requirement for every incoming board member, so every case study and campaign NSPN produces is grounded in the same standard used by prevention professionals across the country.

Research & prevention partners

Science research mentoring

Future Forward Labs

Future Forward Labs is a research academy for pre-college science. It pairs high school students one-on-one with PhD-qualified mentors to develop original research, with guidance on presenting, defending, and publishing their work through science competitions and journals.

Visit website

Volunteering opportunities

Anexa

Anexa is a student-led nonprofit organization connecting students to real community work. Through curated volunteering opportunities, Anexa helps young people find meaningful ways to serve their communities, reaching more than 800,000 students across 20+ countries.

Visit website

Student-led nonprofit organization

In The Beginning

In The Beginning is a Chicago-born, nationwide student-led nonprofit organization supporting young refugees and displaced students. Through academic tutoring, creative arts classes, mentoring, cultural immersion, and community exploration, it gives students a welcoming, safe space to build confidence, find belonging, and look to the future with hope.

What We Do

Everything we runstarts with the research.

Our work is grounded in research and public health data—not assumptions. We draw on trusted sources, including the CDC, SAMHSA, NIH, and FDA.

01

Evidence-Based Prevention

Our programs are regularly updated to reflect emerging trends in youth substance use and proven prevention strategies. Students get accurate, up-to-date information they can trust.

02

Peer-to-Peer Support

Chapter Leaders use NSPN training and case studies to guide discussions and activities with their peers. Students build practical skills for making healthy decisions, navigating peer pressure, and responding to challenging situations.

03

Community Outreach

Chapters bring prevention beyond the classroom through awareness campaigns, events, and connections with their schools and communities. Members can earn verified volunteer hours through eligible chapter activities.

Resources

Support & Crisis Resources

If you or someone you know needs help right now, these free, confidential services are available 24/7.

SAMHSA National Helpline

1-800-662-HELP (4357) — free, confidential treatment referral and information, in English and Spanish, 24/7.

Call 1-800-662-4357

988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline

Call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org, for free and confidential support in a suicidal or emotional crisis — 24 hours a day, every day.

Call 988

More resources, including state-specific services, will be added here over time.
